title: Unique representative normalization of the derived constant-tower comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be small sites with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$ and a morphism of ringed topoi $(f,c)$, where $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ is left exact and $c:f^{-1}R\to S$. Put $F(M)=f^{-1}M\otimes_{f^{-1}R}S$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Use the module categories and derived localizations $Q,Q'$ of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and strict towers indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Choose universal total left-derived pairs $(L,\varepsilon)$ for $Q'F$ and $(\widetilde L,\tau)$ for its levelwise tower functor. Universality and computation are as in [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class], using the objectwise K-flat flat-term class of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements]. All formulas below include the canonical exact-functor localization identifications. Let $\Delta,\Delta'$ be the exact constant-tower functors and their termwise derived functors [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. There is a unique natural isomorphism $b:\Delta'L\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde L\Delta$ such that for every K-flat flat-term $P$,
$$\tau_{\Delta P}b_{QP}=\Delta'(\varepsilon_P),$$
where $F(\Delta P)=\Delta'F(P)$. In particular $b_{QP}=\tau_{\Delta P}^{-1}\Delta'(\varepsilon_P)$.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes (dual); parent blueprint completed-pullback invocation, item Step 4 constant-tower subargument.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $\mathcal A'=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$, and distinguish the complex/homotopy constant-tower functors $\Delta_K,\Delta'_K$ from their induced derived functors $\Delta_D,\Delta'_D$. Kernels and cokernels of towers are levelwise, so a constant short exact sequence is short exact; hence $\Delta,\Delta'$ are exact. Apply exact-functor derived factorization to obtain $\Delta_D Q\cong Q_{\mathrm{Tow}}\Delta_K$ and $\Delta'_D Q'\cong Q'_{\mathrm{Tow}}\Delta'_K$. Termwise module pullback of a constant tower has all levels $F(P)$ and identity transitions, so $\widetilde F\Delta_K=\Delta'_K F$, naturally on complexes and homotopy classes. Set $U=\Delta'_D L$ and $V=\widetilde L\Delta_D$; from now on use the preceding canonical identifications in their components.

Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of K-flat complexes with flat terms. The diagram-replacement theorem with the one-object category gives, for every complex $X$, a quasi-isomorphism $P\to X$ with $P\in\mathcal P$. Its tower version gives the resolving class of objectwise K-flat flat-term tower complexes, and $\Delta_KP$ belongs to this class because every evaluation is $P$. The same theorem says that pullback inverts quasi-isomorphisms between objects of these respective classes. The resolving-class derived-functor theorem therefore makes $\varepsilon_P$ and $T_P:=\tau_{\Delta_KP}$ invertible. This applies to the chosen universal pairs: compare each with the pair supplied by that theorem using universality in both directions; uniqueness makes the composites identities and the comparison preserves the counit. Put $E_P=\Delta'_D(\varepsilon_P):U(QP)\to Q'_{\mathrm{Tow}}\Delta'_KF(P)$ and $a_P=T_P^{-1}E_P:U(QP)\to V(QP)$. Both factors are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, dual part; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 077J and 0G7E as packaged by the cited strict-diagram node

proof.text:
For any homotopy-category morphism $t:P\to P'$ between objects of $\mathcal P$, put $H(t)=Q'_{\mathrm{Tow}}\Delta'_KF(t)$. Naturality of the two counits gives $T_{P'}V(Qt)=H(t)T_P$ and $E_{P'}U(Qt)=H(t)E_P$. Consequently
$$T_{P'}V(Qt)a_P=H(t)E_P=E_{P'}U(Qt)=T_{P'}a_{P'}U(Qt).$$
Cancel the isomorphism $T_{P'}$ to get $V(Qt)a_P=a_{P'}U(Qt)$. Thus the explicitly defined $a_P$ is natural on the full resolving class. This calculation uses the counits of the chosen pairs, not a comparison chosen without its counit.

source.place: Tag 06XN, computation on the resolving class; explicit counit naturality calculation

proof.text: In $K(\mathcal A)$ the quasi-isomorphisms $W$ admit a right calculus of fractions and $Q$ is their localization. Apply the resolving-class extension lemma with source $K(\mathcal A)$, target $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A'))$, resolving predicate $\mathcal P$, functors $UQ,VQ$, and components $a_P$. Its resolution hypothesis is Step 2, its naturality hypothesis is Step 3, and $UQ$ inverts $W$ because $Q$ does. It supplies a natural transformation $\gamma:UQ\to VQ$ with $\gamma_P=a_P$. The homotopy-category objects here are the same underlying complexes; the replacements of Step 2 give the required morphisms in that category.

source.place: Tag 04VC, definition-multiplicative-system, right Ore axioms; derived.tex Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic; resolving-class extension supplied by lem-sc-nattrans-from-resolving-class

proof.text:
For a resolution $s:P\to X$ as in Step 2, naturality of $\gamma$ gives
$$\gamma_X=V(Qs)a_PU(Qs)^{-1}.$$
Every factor is invertible, since $Qs$ is invertible. Thus $\gamma$ is a natural isomorphism (inverting its naturality squares gives the naturality of its componentwise inverse). Both $UQ$ and $VQ$ invert quasi-isomorphisms and are already lifts of $U,V$ along $Q$. Apply the natural-isomorphism lifting clause of the localization universal-property node to obtain $b:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ with $b_{QX}=\gamma_X$. At $P\in\mathcal P$ this yields $b_{QP}=T_P^{-1}E_P$, so $\tau_{\Delta P}b_{QP}=\Delta'(\varepsilon_P)$ as required.

source.place: Tag 04VK, lemma-properties-right-localization; natural-transformation enhancement in Mathlib CategoryTheory/Localization/Predicate.lean, liftNatIso and liftNatTrans_app

proof.text:
Let $c:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ satisfy the displayed normalization. Cancelling $T_P$ gives $c_{QP}=a_P=b_{QP}$ for every $P\in\mathcal P$. For any complex $X$, choose $s:P\to X$ as in Step 2. Naturality of $b,c$ gives
$$c_{QX}=V(Qs)c_{QP}U(Qs)^{-1}=V(Qs)b_{QP}U(Qs)^{-1}=b_{QX}.$$
The faithfulness clause (3) of the localization universal-property node makes $c=b$ on the derived category. Equality of natural isomorphisms follows from equality of their forward transformations. This proves uniqueness under exactly the representative normalization in the statement, without imposing a counit equation on non-K-flat complexes.
